[He does not join] the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha...
He applies all phenomena through the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), yet he does not perceive even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*).
Practicing in this way, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [practices] wisdom—
He should be said to be engaged in the perfection [of wisdom].

Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not associate the Buddha with omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), nor does he perceive the Buddha at all; nor [does he perceive] all...

He does not join the knowledge of all aspects with the Buddha, for he does not even perceive the knowledge of all aspects itself. He does not join awakening with the knowledge of all aspects, for he does not even perceive awakening itself. He does not join the knowledge of all aspects with awakening, for he does not even perceive the knowledge of all aspects itself.
For what reason?
The Buddha himself is omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), and omniscience itself is the Buddha.
Awakening (*bodhi*) itself is omniscience, and omniscience itself is awakening.
Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who applies himself in this way should be said to be "engaged in the perfection of wisdom.
[Thus concludes the instruction on the Jewel of the Buddha.]

Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not apply the thought that "form comes into being," nor does he apply the thought that "form ceases to be. He does not apply the thought that "feeling comes into being," nor does he apply the thought that "feeling ceases to be."
He does not apply himself to the thought that "perception comes into being," nor does he apply himself to the thought that "perception ceases to be.
He does not apply himself to the thought that "formative forces come into being," nor does he apply himself to the thought that "formative forces cease to be.
He does not apply himself to the thought that "consciousness comes into being," nor does he apply himself to the thought that "consciousness ceases to be."
One does not associate form with being permanent,
nor does one associate form with being impermanent;
one does not associate form with being pleasant, nor...
One applies the thought, "Form is suffering.

One does not apply the thought, "Form is the self," nor does one apply the thought, "Form is not-self. One does not apply the thought, "Form is peaceful," nor does one apply the thought, "Form is not peaceful."

He does not apply [the notion] that feeling is permanent, nor does he apply [the notion] that feeling is impermanent; he does not apply [the notion] that feeling is pleasure, nor does he apply [the notion] that feeling is suffering;
he does not apply [the notion] that feeling is self, nor does he apply [the notion] that feeling is non-self.
He does not associate feeling with "peace," nor does he associate feeling with "non-peace. He does not associate perception with "permanence," nor does he associate perception with "impermanence";
he does not associate perception with "happiness," nor does he associate perception with "suffering."
One does not associate perception with "self," nor does one associate perception with "non-self.
One does not associate perception with "peaceful," nor does one associate perception with "not peaceful.
One does not associate volitional formations with "permanent," nor does one associate volitional formations with "impermanent."
Thus he applies himself;
he does not apply himself to the thought that "formations are pleasant," nor does he apply himself to the thought that "formations are painful."
He does not associate [the mind] with the thought that "formations are the self," nor does he associate them with the thought that "formations are non-self";
he does not associate them with the thought that "formations are peaceful."
He does not associate formative forces with being unpeaceful.
He does not associate consciousness with being permanent, nor does he associate consciousness with being impermanent.
He does not associate consciousness with being happiness, nor does he associate consciousness with being suffering.

One does not apply the thought that "consciousness is the self," nor does one apply the thought that "consciousness is not the self. One does not apply the thought that "consciousness is peaceful," nor does one apply the thought that "consciousness is not peaceful. One does not apply the thought that "form is empty," nor does one apply the thought that "form is not empty."

He does not course with the thought that "form has signs," nor does he course with the thought that "form is signless. He does not course with the thought that "form has aspirations," nor does he course with the thought that "form is aspirationless."
He does not practice with the thought that "feeling is empty," nor does he practice with the thought that "feeling is not empty";
he does not practice with the thought that "feeling has signs," nor... [does he practice with the thought that feeling is signless].

Or he does not course in the thought that "feeling is signless," nor does he course in the thought that "feeling is with aspiration," nor does he course in the thought that "feeling is without aspiration."
He does not course in the notion that "perception is empty," nor does he course in the notion that "perception is not empty.
He does not course in the notion that "perception has signs," nor does he course in the notion that "perception is signless.
He does not course in the notion that "perception is with aspiration," nor does he course in the notion that "perception is without aspiration."
He does not practice with the thought that "formations are empty," nor does he practice with the thought that "formations are not empty.
He does not practice with the thought that "formations have signs," nor does he practice with the thought that "formations are signless."
He does not practice with the thought that "formative forces are with aspiration," nor does he practice with the thought that "formative forces are without aspiration.
He does not apply the notion that "consciousness is empty," nor does he apply the notion that "consciousness is not empty.
He does not practice with the thought that "consciousness has signs," nor does he practice with the thought that "consciousness is signless."
He does not course with the thought that "consciousness is with aspiration," nor does he course with the thought that "consciousness is without aspiration.

He who courses in this manner does not approach the idea that "he courses in the perfection of wisdom," nor does he approach the idea that "he does not course"; he neither courses nor does he not course.

He does not approach [the thought] "he courses," nor does he approach "he does not course at all," nor does he approach "he neither courses nor does not course. Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in this manner is to be called one who is engaged in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva courses in the perfection of wisdom, he does not...
He practices the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of generosity;
he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of ethical discipline.
He does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of patience;
he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of vigor.

He does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of meditation; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of wisdom; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the stage of non-retrogression.
He does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the maturation of sentient beings;
he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the purification of a buddha-field.
He does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the ten powers of a Tathāgata;
he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four grounds of self-confidence.

He does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four analytical knowledges; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; nor [for the sake of] the internal...
He practices the perfection of wisdom for the sake of internal emptiness; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of external emptiness;
nor for the sake of internal-and-external emptiness.
He does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of that [emptiness]; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of emptiness;
nor for the sake of the great emptiness.
He practices the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the conditioned; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of the ultimate;
he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of the conditioned.
He does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of absolute emptiness;
he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of emptiness without beginning or end; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of emptiness of non-dispersal.
One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of all phenomena.

One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of specific characteristics; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of non-apprehension.
One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of non-existence by way of its intrinsic nature,
nor does one practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of existence.
One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of non-existence;
one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of other-nature.
One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of suchness;
one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the realm of phenomena; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the limit of reality.
For what reason?
Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom does not perceive the differentiation of any dharma whatsoever.
In this way, Śāriputra,
a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the divine eye.
One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the divine ear;
one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the knowledge of others' minds.
One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of recollecting former abodes;
one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the various types of supernormal power.
For what reason?
Because, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, one does not even perceive the perfection of wisdom itself; how much less [could one perceive anything else]?
How much less could one speak of a bodhisattva possessing all aspects or all superknowledges?
For it is in this way, Śāriputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom is to be called "engaged."
Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, it does not occur to him:
"With my divine eye, in the eastern direction, in worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges..."
"I shall know the death and rebirth of sentient beings in the world-systems," "I shall hear their sounds with the divine ear," and "I shall know their very minds"—
as well as [their] former abodes.
"Having recollected this, I shall go by means of supernatural power and teach the Dharma"—
it does not occur to a bodhisattva mahāsattva in this way, Śāriputra.

"I shall, with the divine eye, know the passing away and rebirth of beings in world-systems in the southern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; with the divine ear, I shall hear their sounds; I shall know their very minds;
and having traveled by means of supernatural power and recollected their former abodes, I shall teach them the Dharma."
In this way, Śāriputra, it does not occur to a bodhisattva mahāsattva:

"With my divine eye, I shall know the death and rebirth of beings in world-systems in the western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges," or "With my divine ear, I shall hear their sounds," or "I shall know their very minds."
"And having recollected their very former abodes, I shall go by means of supernatural power and teach them the Dharma"—

thus it is, Śāriputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not think: "With my divine eye, I shall know the passing away and rebirth of beings in world-systems in the northern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges," or "With my divine ear, I shall hear their sounds."
"I shall know their very minds;
and having gone by means of supernormal power and recollecting their very past lives, I shall teach them the Dharma"—
Śāriputra, it does not occur to a bodhisattva mahāsattva in this way.

"I shall know, with the divine eye, the passing away and rebirth of beings in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northeastern direction; I shall hear their sounds with the divine ear; I shall know their very minds;
and having gone by means of supernatural power, I shall teach the Dharma to them after recollecting their own former abodes."

In this way, Śāriputra, it does not occur to a bodhisattva mahāsattva: "With my divine eye, I shall know the death and rebirth of beings in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the eastern direction"; nor does he think: "With my divine ear, I shall hear their sounds," or "I shall know their very minds."
"And having recalled their very former abodes, I shall go by means of miraculous power and teach the Dharma.
In this way, Śāriputra, it does not occur to a bodhisattva mahāsattva:
"With my divine eye, [I shall see] the sentient beings in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southern-western direction..."

"I shall know death and rebirth," "I shall hear their sounds with the divine ear," "I shall know their very minds," "and having recollected their past abodes and traveled by means of supernormal power, I shall teach them the Dharma"—
Śāriputra, it does not occur to a bodhisattva mahāsattva in this way.

"I shall know, with the divine eye, the passing away and rebirth of beings in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges river in the northwestern direction; I shall hear their sounds with the divine ear; I shall know their very minds;
and having gone by means of supernatural power and recollecting their past lives, I shall teach them the Dharma."

In this way, Śāriputra, it does not occur to a bodhisattva mahāsattva: "With my divine eye, I shall know the death and rebirth of beings in world systems in the downward direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges"; nor does he think: "With my divine ear, I shall hear their sounds," or "I shall know their very minds."
"Having recollected their very former abodes and having gone there by means of supernatural power, I shall teach the Dharma"—
Śāriputra, it does not occur to a bodhisattva mahāsattva in this way:
"I [shall see with] the divine eye."

"Thinking, 'I shall know the death and rebirth of sentient beings in world-systems in the upward direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges,' and 'With my divine ear, I shall hear their sounds,' and 'I shall know their very minds.'"
And having recollected their very own former abodes and gone there by means of supernatural power, I shall teach the Dharma.
It is in this way, Śāriputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom [will bring about] immeasurable—
He should be said to be "engaged" while bringing immeasurable and incalculable beings to final nirvāṇa.
For it is thus, Śāriputra, that Māra the Evil One finds no opportunity to gain entry against a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in the perfection of wisdom.
And all other worldly afflictions whatsoever that he may have are entirely shattered.
Moreover, Śāriputra, those Buddhas in the eastern direction—
The Blessed Ones who reside, remain, and maintain themselves in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges,
and who teach the Dharma; and those who are their disciples, and those who are Pratyekabuddhas,
and those who are gods belonging to the retinue of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa, the Yāma, the Tuṣita, and the Nirmāṇarati [heavens].
The Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, the Brahmapārṣadyas, the Brahmapurohitas, the Mahābrahmans, the Parīttābhas, the Apramāṇābhas, the Ābhāsvaras, the Parīttaśubhas, the Apramāṇaśubhas,
the Śubhakṛtsnas, the Anabhrakas, the Puṇyaprasavas, the Bṛhatphalas, the Asaṃjñisattvas, the Śuddhāvāsas, and the Avṛhas.

The Ātapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha gods also protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking: "May no one whatsoever create an obstacle for this bodhisattva mahāsattva. Furthermore, whatever physical defects he may have, these too become merely matters of the present life.
For what reason? Because he pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness. Furthermore, Śāriputra, those in the southern direction...
The Buddha-Bhagavāns reside, remain, and maintain themselves in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges,

teaching the Dharma; and those who are their śrāvakas, those who are pratyekabuddhas, and those who are gods of the Cāturmahārājakāyika, Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, Paranirmitavaśavartin, and Brahmakāyika realms.
The Brahmapurohita gods, the Mahābrahmans, the Parīttābhas, the Apramāṇābhas, the Ābhāsvaras, the Parīttaśubhas, the Apramāṇaśubhas,

the Śubhakṛtsnas, the Anabhrakas, the Puṇyaprasavas, the Bṛhatphalas, the Asaṃjñisattvas, the Śuddhāvāsa gods— the Avṛhas, the Atapas, the Sudṛśas, the Sudarśanas, and the Akaniṣṭhas— they too protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
May no one whatsoever create an obstacle for this bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Whatever physical defects he may have, they shall become manifest in this very life.
Why is that?

For he pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness. Śāriputra, those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who reside, stay, and maintain themselves in the world systems of the western direction— numerous as the sands of the river Ganges— and who teach the Dharma, as well as their disciples...

And those who are Pratyekabuddhas; and those who are the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin [heavens]; the Brahmapārṣadya, Brahmapurohita, and Mahābrahmā [Brahma-worlds]; the Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, and Ābhāsvara [Abhāsvara-heavens]; the Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Śubhakṛtsna [Śubhakṛtsna-heavens]; the Anabhraka, Puṇyaprasava, and Bṛhatphala [Bṛhatphala-heavens].
The non-percipient beings, the Śuddhāvāsa deities— the Avṛhas, Atapas, Sudṛśas, Sudarśanas, and Akaniṣṭhas— they too protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva,
thinking: "May no one whatsoever cause any obstacle for this bodhisattva mahāsattva."
Whatever physical defects he may have, they too become manifest only in this present life.
Why is that?
Because he pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness.

Moreover, Śāriputra, those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who in the northern direction reside, stay, and maintain themselves in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, and who teach the Dharma; and their disciples; and the pratyekabuddhas;
and the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa, the Yāma, the Tuṣita, the Nirmāṇarati, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin [heavens]—[all these hear this Dharma].

The gods of the Brahma-pārṣadya, Brahma-purohita, Mahābrahmā; the Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, and Ābhāsvara; the Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Śubhakṛtsna; the Anabhraka, Puṇyaprasava, and Bṛhatphala; the Asaṃjñisattva; and the Śuddhāvāsa gods—the Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha—they too protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
May no one whatsoever create an obstacle for this bodhisattva mahāsattva;
even those bodily defects he may have shall become merely matters pertaining to the present life.
Why is that?
For he pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness.
Moreover, Śāriputra, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside in the world-systems of the northeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—
They remain, they endure, they persist, and they teach the Dharma;
and those who are their disciples,
and those who are pratyekabuddhas, and those gods from the Cāturmahārājakāyika realm up to the Akaniṣṭha realm.
Even those gods provide protection for that bodhisattva mahāsattva,
thinking: "May no obstacle indeed arise for this bodhisattva mahāsattva."
"Moreover, Śāriputra, those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who in the southeastern direction— equal in number to the sands of the river Ganges— dwell, remain, and maintain themselves,

and teach the Dharma; and their śrāvakas, and their pratyekabuddhas, and the gods from the Cāturmahārājakāyika realm up to the Akaniṣṭha gods— they too shall provide protection for that bodhisattva mahāsattva."
"May there indeed be no obstacle for this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

Śāriputra, those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who dwell, remain, and maintain themselves in the world systems of the south-western direction—numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—and who teach the Dharma;

and those who are their disciples, and those who are Pratyekabuddhas, and those who are gods from the Cāturmahārājakāyika realm up to the Akaniṣṭha gods—they too shall provide protection for that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
"May there indeed be no obstacle for this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva!
May there indeed be no obstacle for this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva!

Furthermore, Śāriputra, those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who reside, remain, and maintain themselves in the world-systems of the northwestern direction—numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—and who teach the Dharma; [they all protect him]."

And those who are their disciples, and those who are pratyekabuddhas, and those who are the gods of the Cāturmahārājakāyika realm up to the Akaniṣṭha gods— they too provide protection for that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking, "May no obstacle whatsoever befall this bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who reside, remain, and maintain themselves in the world systems in the direction below, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, and who teach the Dharma— [they also provide protection].

And those who are their disciples, and those who are pratyekabuddhas, and those who are gods belonging to the Four Great Kings, up to the Akaniṣṭha gods— they too shall provide protection for that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking, "May no obstacle whatsoever befall this bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who reside, stay, and maintain themselves in the world systems of the upward direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, and who teach the Dharma— [they too shall protect him].

And those who are his disciples, and those who are pratyekabuddhas, and those who are gods belonging to the realm of the Four Great Kings, up to the Akaniṣṭha gods— they too shall provide protection for that bodhisattva mahāsattva,
thinking, "May no obstacle whatsoever befall this bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, there is little—
With effort, the gateways of the dhāraṇīs and the gateways of the samādhis become manifest before him;
and in all places of rebirth, he pleases the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas,
such that he is never at any time separated from the Blessed Buddhas until he has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
In this way, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom should be said to be "engaged.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, as a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in the perfection of wisdom, [he should be said to be engaged].
It is not so. There is no such dharma that is either conjoined with or disjoined from other dharmas.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, it does not occur to him:
"I might or might not quickly awaken to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu)."
For what reason?
Because the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) is not fully awakened to by means of the realm of phenomena.
It is in this way, Śāriputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom is said to be "engaged."
Furthermore,

Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom does not perceive anything as distinct from the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), nor does he perceive any diversity of phenomena within the realm of phenomena.
He performs the act of doing;
nor does it occur to him that "this realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) is thus penetrated" or "it is not penetrated."
For he does not perceive any phenomenon by which he might penetrate that true nature of phenomena;
for he does not [perceive] the realm of phenomena as empty.
He does not apply [the mind] to what is non-empty;
thus, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom is to be called "engaged."

Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not associate the eye-element with emptiness, nor does he associate emptiness with the eye-element. He does not associate the form-element with emptiness, nor does he associate emptiness with the form-element. Nor...
One joins the eye-consciousness element with emptiness, but does not join emptiness with the eye-consciousness element;
one does not join the ear element with emptiness, nor does one join emptiness with the ear element.
He does not associate the sound-element with emptiness, nor does he associate emptiness with the sound-element.
He does not associate the ear-consciousness-element with emptiness, nor does he associate emptiness with the ear-consciousness-element.
He does not associate the nose-element with emptiness, nor does he associate emptiness with the nose-element.
He does not associate the odor-element with emptiness, nor does he associate emptiness with the odor-element.
He does not associate the nose-consciousness-element with emptiness, nor does he associate emptiness with the nose-consciousness-element.
He does not associate the tongue-element with emptiness, nor does he associate emptiness with the tongue-element.
He does not associate the taste element with emptiness, nor does he associate emptiness with the taste element.
He does not associate the tongue-consciousness element with emptiness, nor does he associate emptiness with the tongue-consciousness element.
He does not associate the body element with emptiness, nor does he associate emptiness with the body element.
He does not join the tangible element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the tangible element.
He does not join the body-consciousness element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the body-consciousness element.
He does not join the mind element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the mind element.
He does not join the dharma-realm with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the dharma-realm;
he does not join the mind-consciousness-realm with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the mind-consciousness-realm.
Why is that?
For this, Śāriputra, is the supreme application of a bodhisattva mahāsattva,
namely, the application of emptiness.
Moving in emptiness, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva—

He does not fall into the level of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas; he purifies the Buddha-field, brings sentient beings to maturity, and swiftly awakens to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Śāriputra, whatever applications there are for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, of those [the perfection of wisdom is the foremost].
This yoga is declared to be the foremost, the best, the most excellent, the supreme, the unsurpassed, the unequaled, the equal of the unequaled, and the sublime. For what reason?
For this, Śāriputra, is the unsurpassed yoga: namely, the yoga of the perfection of wisdom, the yoga of emptiness, the yoga of the signless, and the yoga of the wishless.
Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices in this way should be known as one who has received the prediction;
he has drawn near to his own prediction.

Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices in this way will accomplish the welfare of immeasurable and incalculable beings, yet it will not occur to him that "the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, will grant me a prophecy."
"I have drawn near to my prediction," "I shall purify a Buddha-field," "I..."
"I shall bring sentient beings to maturity;
having awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment,
I shall turn the wheel of Dharma."
For what reason?
Because he does not isolate the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), nor does he perceive any phenomenon other than the realm of phenomena which [would be] the perfection of wisdom.
Or whoever would practice in the *Amitāyus* [Sūtra], or who might be prophesied by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, for unexcelled, perfect,
and complete enlightenment— for what reason? Because of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
For one practicing in the *Amitāyus* [Sūtra], the perception of a "sentient being" does not arise.
Why is that?
Because, in an ultimate sense, it is so.

A sentient being is neither produced nor ceased, because its nature is non-arising and non-ceasing. And how can that which has neither production nor cessation practice the perfection of wisdom? Practicing in this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom through the non-production of sentient beings.
One practices the perfection of wisdom by means of the emptiness of sentient beings;
one practices the perfection of wisdom by the non-apprehension of sentient beings.
He practices; because of the solitude of sentient beings, he practices in the perfection of wisdom.
For in this way, Śāriputra, the supreme application of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, is namely the application of emptiness, which surpasses all other applications.
He dwells having overcome [all obstacles].
For here, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing this yoga brings forth great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) and does not give rise to a mind of stinginess.
He does not give rise to a mind of immorality; he does not give rise to a mind of malice.
He does not give rise to a lazy mind;
he does not give rise to a distracted mind.
He does not give rise to a mind of faulty wisdom.
[Thus ends the instruction on the Jewel of the Dharma.
When this had been said, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"O Blessed One, whoever..."
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells by means of this dwelling in the perfection of wisdom, from where has he passed away to be reborn here?
Or, having passed away from here, where will he be reborn?
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Śāriputra:
"Śāriputra, that bodhisattva mahāsattva who, by means of this..."
Dwelling by means of the dwelling in the perfection of wisdom, when he passes away from here, he is reborn in this very buddha-field;
or, having passed away from other buddha-fields, or having passed away from the Tuṣita gods, he is reborn here.
[Thus ends the eighth stage of the Bodhisattva.
In this regard, Śāriputra, as for that bodhisattva mahāsattva who, having passed away from among humans, is reborn into the very same class of existence as humans— for that bodhisattva mahāsattva—

Setting aside those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who are subject to regression, their faculties become sluggish; they do not quickly enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom, nor does the gateway of dhāraṇī appear before them, nor the gateway of samādhi.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, as to what you said: "Lord, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva enters into this yoga of the perfection of wisdom, having passed away from here, where will he be reborn?"
Śāriputra, whichever bodhisattva mahāsattva enters into this yoga of the perfection of wisdom will, having passed away from this buddha-field,
proceed from one buddha-field to another.
In that buddha-field, he will honor the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; he shall never be separated from a Buddha.
[Thus is the bodhisattva who follows through faith.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, that bodhisattva mahāsattva who has passed away from other buddha-fields...
When he is reborn here, his faculties become sharp;
he quickly attains this yoga, namely, the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.
Even though he has passed beyond that birth, these most profound dharmas become manifest to him;
subsequently, he applies himself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
He enters into meditative absorption;
wherever he is reborn in a Buddha-field, there he will please the Tathāgatas, the Arhats, the perfectly enlightened Buddhas.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, for that bodhisattva mahāsattva who, having passed away from the Tuṣita gods, has been reborn here, his faculties are even more acute;
the six perfections and all the gateways of dhāraṇīs and samādhis are not lost to him.
And they become manifest.
[Thus is the follower of the Bodhisattva-dharma.
Śāriputra, there are Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who, practicing and striving in the perfection of wisdom,
exerting themselves through the power of skillful means for the sake of maturing sentient beings, realize the fruit of stream-entry—

They do so, yet they do not conceive the thought, "I am a stream-enterer. Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, being unskilled in means, accomplish the four dhyānas while [practicing] the perfections.
And they practice [the path]. By virtue of that attainment of meditative concentration (dhyāna), they are reborn among the long-lived gods.
If, after passing away from there, they are reborn among humans or gods, they will please the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones;
yet even for them, their faculties (indriya) remain dull and not sharp.

“Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who enter into the meditative absorptions and practice the perfection of wisdom; yet, through a lack of skill in means, they relinquish those meditative absorptions and are reborn in the desire realm. For them also, Śāriputra—”
O Śāriputra, the faculties of these Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas are blunt, not sharp.
[Thus ends the description of the one who has entered the second and third fruits, the one liberated through faith.
There are, O Śāriputra, Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who, having produced the four dhyānas, enter into the four immeasurables...

They enter [the meditative states]; they enter the four formless attainments, the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path. These Greatly Compassionate Ones, through skillful means—

They are reborn through skillfulness, not by the power of the dhyānas, nor by the power of the immeasurables, nor by the power of the formless attainments; and they are reborn in those places where they will please the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Furthermore, being never separated from this dwelling in the perfection of wisdom, they remain right here in this Fortunate Aeon.
They will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
[Thus ends the section on those established in the second and third fruits, who have attained vision.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas bound by only one more birth who [dwell] in the perfection of wisdom.

Wandering about with skill in means, they enter the four meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*); they cultivate the foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), the right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*), the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*),
the faculties (*indriya*), the powers (*bala*), the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*), and the path (*mārga*).
They enter the concentration on emptiness;
they enter the concentration on the signless;
they enter the concentration on the wishless.

And they do not fall under their influence; rather, having pleased the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who have appeared before them, and having practiced the holy life there, they are reborn once again among the Tuṣita gods to share in their company.
There, they remain for as long as their lifespan lasts.

Having remained there for the duration of their lifespan with unimpaired faculties, mindful and clearly comprehending, surrounded and honored by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of gods, they manifest rebirth here and attain unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in various buddha-fields.
They understand.
[Thus is the once-returner.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the six superknowledges and who are not reborn in the desire realm, nor in the form realm, nor in the formless realm.
Moreover, they travel from buddha-field to buddha-field, honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the six superknowledges; sporting with those superknowledges, they travel from buddhafield to buddhafield,
to those buddhafields where there is no designation of the vehicle of the śrāvakas or the pratyekabuddhas.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the six superknowledges (abhijñā);

sporting with those superknowledges, they travel from buddha-field to buddha-field, to those buddha-fields where the lifespan is immeasurable. Furthermore, Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the six superknowledges...
They travel from world-system to world-system; having gone there, they remain in places where the sound of "Buddha" is not heard,
nor the sound of "Dharma," nor the sound of "Saṅgha," and there they cause the sounds of "Buddha," "Dharma," and "Saṅgha" to be heard by sentient beings.
And they speak the praises of the Three Jewels;
by means of that sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," and the sound of "Saṅgha," when they pass away from there, they are reborn wherever there are Buddha-Bhagavats.

[Thus is the non-returner. Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, having produced the four dhyānas, enter the four immeasurables and the four formless attainments, and they are endowed with skill in means.

Having emerged from their meditative concentrations and attainments, they are reborn in the desire realm; for the sake of maturing sentient beings, they are born into great kṣatriya families, or great brahmin families, or great householder families.
[Thus, this is the family of the human clan.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who enter the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
By the power of skillful means, or by the force of their meditative absorptions, concentrations, and attainments, they are also reborn into the company of the gods of the Four Great Kings.
They are reborn into the fellowship of the gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāmas, the Tuṣitas, the Nirmāṇaratis, and the Paranirmitavaśavartins;
remaining there, they bring sentient beings to maturity and purify the buddha-field.

And they please the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones. Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, having produced the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, [enter them].
They fall [from there]. Having passed away from that state, through skill in means (*upāyakauśalya*), they are reborn in the Brahma-world as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven.
There, they become Brahmas, Great Brahmas, within those Brahma-palaces.
They remain there; having remained there, they travel from buddha-field to buddha-field,
and they entreat those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who are in those buddha-fields to turn the wheel of Dharma.
[Thus ends the section on the family of the gods.

06509 Śāriputra, there are bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who have attained the four dhyānas, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma), and they practice for the sake of conforming to them. Of these four—
Those who have attained the noble truths but do not yet penetrate them should be known as bodhisattva-mahāsattvas bound by only one more birth.
[Thus is one who is not subject to the interval.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, who, from the first production of the thought of awakening, become attainers of the four dhyānas.
They become attainers of the four immeasurables; they become attainers of the four formless attainments;
[they become attainers] of the foundations of mindfulness and the right efforts—

They cultivate the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path; they attain the powers, the grounds of self-confidence, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha.
Through skill in means, they are reborn among the gods of the Brahma-realm up to the Akaniṣṭha gods; and there,
having fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, they [attain it].
They act for the benefit of sentient beings.
[Thus is the one who attains parinirvāṇa in the intermediate state.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, by the very first production of the thought of awakening, fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Having turned the wheel of Dharma and accomplished the welfare of immeasurable and incalculable beings,
they pass into final nirvana in the realm of nirvana without remainder; for them who have thus passed away,
the True Dharma remains for an eon or the remainder of an eon.
[Thus is the one who attains parinirvāṇa upon rebirth.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, while practicing the six perfections, pass from world-system to world-system.
And there they shall establish sentient beings in awakening.

Constantly exerting themselves for the sake of sentient beings, they never speak words that are unbeneficial. Constantly exerting themselves for the sake of sentient beings, they travel from buddha-field to buddha-field.

Those bodhisattva mahāsattvas, for the sake of sentient beings, after incalculable and immeasurable eons, awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in various buddha-fields. [Thus is the one who attains parinirvāṇa with effort.]

"Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, by the very first production of the thought of awakening, enter the bodhisattva's path of certainty, or they abide on the stage of non-retrogression,
[attaining] all the qualities of a Buddha."
or they fully accomplish it.
“Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, by the very first production of the thought of awakening,
apply themselves to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom;
they [are accompanied] by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas.”
Together with thousands [of bodhisattvas], they travel from buddha-field to buddha-field in order to purify their own buddha-fields;
and in various buddha-fields, they fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. [Thus ends the one who attains parinirvāṇa without exertion.]

"Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, practicing the six perfections, having become universal monarchs and placing the perfection of generosity foremost, shall provide all the requisites for happiness to all sentient beings—
food to those seeking food and drink to those seeking drink."
In this way, they will provide perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, incense, beds, seats, shelters, houses, wealth, grain, jewels, pearls, gold, silver, coral, ornaments,
and the necessities for life.

Having established sentient beings in the ten paths of wholesome action, they are reborn among the gods from the Brahmakāyika realm up to the Akaniṣṭha realm, and in various buddha-fields, they fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
[Thus, there are those for whom Akaniṣṭha is the limit.

Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, having accomplished the four dhyānas, fall away from those dhyānas and, having attained the first dhyāna, are reborn among the gods of the Brahmakāyika heaven. They, moreover—
Having perfected the meditative absorptions and been reborn among the Akaniṣṭha deities, they realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment in various buddha-fields. [Thus ends the "leaper.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, having passed away from the Brahma-world, are reborn in the Śuddhāvāsa heavens. They...
Having bypassed one or two of the Śuddhāvāsa stages, they are reborn among the Akaniṣṭha gods and attain unsurpassed,
perfect enlightenment in various buddha-fields.
[Thus is the "half-leaper.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, having manifested a physical form identical to that of a Tathāgata and having purified the Tuṣita heaven,
are reborn among the gods of the Brahma-realm up to the Akaniṣṭha gods through skillful means.
They teach the Dharma to beings in the hells; they teach the Dharma to beings born in the animal realm; they teach the Dharma to beings in the world of Yama.
There are, Śāriputra, bodhisattvas mahāsattvas...

Those beings who, established in the six perfections, having manifested a physical form identical to that of the Tathāgata’s body, travel to Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā and teach the Dharma to sentient beings, and attend upon the Tathāgatas and perfect the Buddha-fields—
They rejoice and listen to the Dharma.
Likewise in the eastern direction, in the southern, in the western,
in the northern, in the northeastern, in the southeastern, in the southwestern, and in the northwestern [directions].

Above, below, and in all ten directions, having gone to world-systems in each direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings, bring Buddha-fields to completion,
attend upon Buddhas, and listen to the Dharma.
Having emanated emanations from those buddha-fields, they bring forth supreme, distinguished, and unsurpassed buddha-fields.

And those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who are bound to only one more birth, having been reborn in those buddha-fields, realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening in various buddha-fields. [Thus ends the section on passing away from all places.]
06904 Śāriputra, there are bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who, attaining the meditative absorptions and formless attainments, are reborn among the gods of the Brahma-realm up to the Śubhakṛtsna deities.
There, in the sphere of infinite space, up to—
They are reborn at the peak of existence;
from there, they are reborn in various buddha-fields.
[Thus is one who has the peak of existence as his limit.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, having attained the meditative concentrations and formless attainments, are reborn from the sphere of infinite space up to the peak of existence.
Thereafter, they are reborn in various buddha-fields.

[Thus is one who is free from passion for form. Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, while practicing the six perfections, possess bodies adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and are endowed with unsurpassed, completely pure faculties.
They become endowed with those purified faculties and thus become dear and pleasing to many people. Furthermore, those beings who behold those bodhisattva mahāsattvas—

By means of that very clarity of mind, they attain final nirvāṇa through the three vehicles in successive stages. Thus, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should train for the purification of the body, should train for the purification of speech,
and should train for the purification of the mind.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, while practicing the six perfections, obtain refined faculties;
by means of those refined faculties—
Śāriputra,
there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who,
from the first production of the thought of awakening, abiding in the perfection of generosity and the perfection of ethical discipline, never at any time exalt themselves or disparage others.
They do not fall into states of woe, miserable destinies, or perditions until they reach the stage of non-retrogression.

Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, from the first production of the thought of awakening, never abandon the ten paths of wholesome action until they reach the stage of non-retrogression.

"Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, abiding in the perfection of generosity, become universal monarchs (cakravartin) and, having given gifts to sentient beings, establish them precisely upon the ten paths of wholesome action.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, abiding in the perfection of generosity and the perfection of ethical discipline..."
They take possession of hundreds of universal monarchies; they take possession of many hundreds of thousands of universal monarchies.
Abiding therein, [they see] many tens of millions of Buddhas.
They please hundreds of thousands of millions of them,
and they honor, revere, respect, and worship those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
Thereafter, they fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

[Thus is one who attains parinirvāṇa in the present life. Śāriputra, there are bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who, while coursing in the perfection of wisdom, are attainers of the four dhyānas and attainers of the four formless attainments; sporting with these, they first—
They enter the first dhyāna;
then, having emerged from it, they enter the attainment of cessation (nirodhasamāpatti);
then, having emerged from that, they enter the second dhyāna.
Emerging from that, they enter the meditative absorption of cessation;
emerging from that, they enter the third dhyāna.
Emerging from that, they enter the attainment of cessation;
emerging from that,
they enter the fourth dhyāna.
Emerging from that, they enter the attainment of cessation;
emerging from that, they enter the sphere of infinite space.
Emerging from that, they enter the attainment of cessation;
emerging from that, they enter the sphere of infinite consciousness;
emerging from that, they enter the attainment of cessation.
Emerging from that, they enter the sphere of nothingness;
emerging from that, they enter the attainment of cessation.
Emerging from that, they enter the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
emerging from that, they enter the attainment of cessation.

For it is thus, Śāriputra, that bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing in the perfection of wisdom, having entered into a leap-over concentration (avaskandaka-samādhi) through skill in means, fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in various buddha-fields.
[Thus is the one who has realized the body.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, abiding in the six perfections, bring forth the illumination of the Buddha-dharmas for sentient beings.
They themselves also remain never deprived of the radiance of the Buddha-dharmas until they fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
[Thus is one who has entered the path toward arhatship.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, in world-systems devoid of Buddhas and lacking śrāvakas, fully awaken to pratyekabodhi.
Through skill in means, they bring many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of living beings to maturity in the three vehicles and then awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
[Thus ends the section on the Pratyekabuddha.

Śāriputra, there are Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who have attained the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path; as well as the ten powers, the grounds of self-confidence, the analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They are attainers of these dharmas;
yet they do not attain the fruit of stream-entry, nor the fruit of once-returning, nor the fruit of non-returning, nor arhatship, nor do they attain the state of a pratyekabuddha.
Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, they, through skillful means, lead all sentient beings onto the path,
purify them, and cause them to attain the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*) and the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmi*).

They cause others to attain the fruit [of stream-entry], they cause them to attain the fruit of non-returning, they cause them to attain arhatship, and they cause them to attain solitary enlightenment;
without realizing these for themselves, they establish others therein.
[Thus are the fruits obtainable through the paths of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

Śāriputra, whatever is the knowledge and illumination of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, that is but the patience of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has attained the patient acceptance of dharmas without conceptualization (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti). Thus it is said.
To establish others in a Dharma that one has not attained oneself— Śāriputra, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who dwell by means of this perfection of wisdom should be known as irreversible.
"Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, having established themselves in the six perfections, purify the Tuṣita heaven. Furthermore,
those bodhisattva mahāsattvas belong to the Fortunate Aeon (bhadrakalpika)."

These, Śāriputra, are to be known as irreversible bodhisattva-mahāsattvas for whom this arising occurs regarding the qualities of a Buddha. Therefore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva-mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom—
One must not allow any opportunity for faulty actions of body, speech, and mind, and one should train in the complete purification of the actions of body, speech, and mind;
[this is the section on] the irreversible community of bodhisattvas.
[The Illumination. [Thus ends the instruction on the Jewel of the Saṃgha.
When this had been said, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"What, O Blessed One, is..."
"Bodily action is blameworthy, verbal action is blameworthy, and mental action is blameworthy.
When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Śāriputra:
In this regard, Śāriputra, it occurs to a bodhisattva mahāsattva: "What is that body by which I might undertake bodily action? What is that speech by which I might undertake vocal action?"
"What is that mind by which one might initiate mental action?
Examining in this way, he perceives the body, he perceives speech, and he perceives the mind.
Śāriputra,

this undertaking of the physical, verbal, and mental actions of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is faulty. Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [does not perceive it] in the perfection of wisdom.
While practicing, he does not perceive a body, nor does he perceive speech, nor does he perceive a mind; with whatever body, speech,
or mind [he might otherwise act], there is no thought of stinginess, immorality, malice, laziness, distraction, or faulty wisdom.
One would not produce it.
Śāriputra, it is impossible, it is out of the question, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should produce corruption of body, speech, or mind. This is not so.
Such a state exists.
For what reason? Because, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [dwells] in the six...
Practicing the perfections, he purifies the corruption of body, purifies the corruption of speech, and purifies the corruption of mind. Śāriputra said:
“Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva purify the depravity of body, speech, and mind?
The Blessed One replied:
Because, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not apprehend the body, does not apprehend speech, and does not apprehend the mind;
it is in this way, Śāriputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva purifies the corruption of body, speech, and mind. If...
Furthermore, Śāriputra, from the first production of the thought of awakening, ten virtuous paths of action follow the bodhisattva mahāsattva;
and he does not give rise to the mind of a śrāvaka or the mind of a pratyekabuddha.
And for him, a mind of great compassion toward all sentient beings is constantly and continuously present.
Śāriputra, it is in this way that I say the corruption of body, speech, and mind of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is purified.
"Śāriputra, there are bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, who, while practicing the perfection of wisdom and purifying the path to awakening, practice the perfection of generosity;
they practice the perfection of ethical discipline."
They practice the perfection of patience;
they practice the perfection of vigor;
they practice the perfection of meditation.
[They] practice the perfection of wisdom.
Śāriputra said: "Which one, Blessed One—"
[This is] the path to enlightenment for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
The Blessed One said:
"When, Śāriputra,"
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not apprehend the body, he does not apprehend speech,
and he does not apprehend the mind.
One does not perceive the perfection of generosity; one does not perceive the perfection of ethical discipline;
one does not perceive the perfection of patience.
He does not perceive the perfection of vigor; he does not perceive the perfection of meditation;
he does not perceive the perfection of wisdom.
One does not perceive a śrāvaka; one does not perceive a pratyekabuddha.
One does not perceive a bodhisattva;
one does not perceive a Buddha.
This, Śāriputra, is [the nature] of a bodhisattva.

The path to enlightenment for a bodhisattva mahāsattva is this: namely, the non-apprehension of all phenomena. Traveling by this path, the bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the six perfections cannot be overcome.
[Thus ends the instruction on incapacity.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the six perfections does not conceive of form.
He does not conceive of feeling; he does not conceive of perception; he does not conceive of mental formations.
He does not conceive of consciousness;
he does not conceive of the earth element;
he does not conceive of the water element.
He does not conceive of the fire element.
He does not conceive of the wind element; he does not conceive of the space element;
he does not conceive of the consciousness element.
He does not conceive of the eye element; he does not conceive of the form element;
he does not conceive of the eye-consciousness element.
He does not conceive of the ear element;
he does not conceive of the sound element; he does not conceive of the ear-consciousness element.
He does not conceive of the nose element;
he does not conceive of the odor element;
he does not conceive of the nose-consciousness element.
He does not conceive of the tongue element; he does not conceive of the taste element;
he does not conceive of the tongue-consciousness element.
He does not conceive of the body element; he does not conceive of the tangible object element;
he does not conceive of the body-consciousness element.
He does not conceive of the mind-element; he does not conceive of the phenomena-element;
he does not conceive of the mind-consciousness-element.
He does not conceive of the applications of mindfulness; he does not conceive of the right efforts; he does not conceive of the bases of psychic power.
He does not conceive of the sense faculties; he does not conceive of the powers; he does not conceive of the factors of enlightenment.
He does not conceive of the path;
he does not conceive of the perfection of generosity; he does not conceive of the perfection of ethical discipline.
He does not conceive of the perfection of patience; he does not conceive of the perfection of vigor;
he does not conceive of the perfection of meditation.
He does not conceive of the perfection of wisdom;
he does not conceive of the grounds of self-confidence.
He does not conceive of the analytical knowledges; he does not conceive of the ten powers of a Tathāgata;
he does not conceive of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
He does not conceive of the fruit of stream-entry, nor the fruit of once-returning, nor the fruit of non-returning.
He does not conceive of arhatship;
he does not conceive of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; he does not conceive of a bodhisattva.
He conceives of the mahāsattva,
but he does not conceive of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
For it is thus, Śāriputra.

The bodhisattva mahāsattva increases by means of the six perfections and cannot be crushed by anything. Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, abiding in the perfection of wisdom, [attain] omniscience.
They fulfill [these perfections] by means of that wisdom endowed with which all doors to the lower realms are closed for those who possess it.
Nor do they experience the misfortune of human poverty, nor do they assume such a physical form by which they would become objects of reproach among the world including the gods.
[Thus ends the instruction on indefatigability.
Śāriputra said:
"Blessed One, what is the omniscient knowledge of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
The Blessed One said:
"Endowed with that wisdom, a bodhisattva mahāsattva beholds, in the eastern direction, as many Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā."
He hears the teaching of the Dharma and attends upon the Saṃgha;
he beholds the purification of the Buddha-fields.

In this same way, in the southern, western, northern, and intermediate directions, as well as below and above, in each direction [he beholds as many fields] as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā.
He beholds the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas; he hears their teaching of the Dharma and attends upon the Saṅgha;
and he beholds the purity of the Buddha-fields.
By means of that wisdom possessed by the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, there is no [limit to] the Buddhas—
There arises the perception [of this], but not the perception of awakening, nor the perception of a disciple.
There is no perception of a pratyekabuddha;
there is no perception of a self;
there is no perception of another.
There is no perception of a Buddha-field for the bodhisattva mahāsattva who, endowed with that knowledge,
practices the perfection of giving.
He practices the perfection of ethical discipline;
he practices the perfection of patience;
he practices the perfection of vigor.
He practices the perfection of meditation;
he practices the perfection of wisdom,
yet he does not apprehend the perfection.
Endowed with which knowledge a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates the applications of mindfulness and yet does not apprehend the applications of mindfulness;

he cultivates the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path, and yet [does not apprehend] the right efforts, the bases of psychic power...
He perceives the powers of the feet, the faculties, the factors of awakening, and the path;

he fully accomplishes the powers, the grounds of self-confidence, and the unique qualities of a Buddha, yet he does not perceive those powers, grounds of self-confidence, or unique qualities of a Buddha. This is...
Śāriputra, it is the knowledge of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; endowed with which knowledge,
a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills all the qualities of a buddha,
yet does not conceive of those qualities of a buddha as real.
[Thus concludes the instruction on the thorough acquisition of the practice.
Śāriputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who obtain and purify the five eyes.
What are the five? Namely, the fleshly eye, the divine eye, the wisdom eye, the Dharma eye, and the Buddha eye.
Śāriputra said:
"Blessed One, what is the perfectly pure flesh-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva? The Blessed One replied,
"Śāriputra, there is indeed a flesh-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva."
Śāriputra, there is the fleshly eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva that sees for one hundred yojanas;
there is [also] that which sees for two hundred yojanas.
"Śāriputra, there is the fleshly eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva which sees Jambudvīpa;
Śāriputra, there is the fleshly eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva which sees a world-system of four continents."
"Śāriputra, there is the fleshly eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva which sees a thousandfold world system;
Śāriputra, there is the fleshly eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva which sees a two-thousandfold world system;
Śāriputra, there is the fleshly eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva which sees a three-thousandfold great..."
He sees a thousandfold world system.
Śāriputra, this is the purified flesh-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Śāriputra said:
"Blessed One, what is the perfectly pure divine eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva? The Blessed One replied:
Śāriputra, that which is the divine eye of the gods of the Four Great Kings, that a bodhisattva fully knows;
and that which belongs to the gods of the Thirty-three.
The Bodhisattva understands that divine eye which belongs to the Yāma gods;
the Bodhisattva understands that divine eye which belongs to the Tuṣita gods.
The divine eye of the Nirmāṇarati gods, that the Bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, that the Bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Brahmakāyika gods, that the Bodhisattva understands.
The divine eye of the Brahmapurohita gods, that the Bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Brahmapārṣadya gods, that the Bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Parīttābha gods, that the Bodhisattva understands.
The divine eye of the Apramāṇābha gods, that the bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Ābhāsvara gods, that the bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Śubhakṛtsna gods, that the bodhisattva understands.
The divine eye of the Anabhraka gods, that the bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Puṇyaprasava gods, that the bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Bṛhatphala gods, that the bodhisattva understands.
The divine eye of the gods who are non-percipient beings, that the bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Śuddhāvāsa gods, that the bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Aspr̥ha gods, that the bodhisattva understands.
The divine eye of the Atapa gods, the Bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Sudṛśa gods, the Bodhisattva understands;
the divine eye of the Sudarśana gods, the Bodhisattva understands.
The divine eye of the Akaniṣṭha gods is what the bodhisattva understands;
however, Śāriputra, the divine eye of the bodhisattva mahāsattva is not understood by the gods belonging to the retinue of the Four Great Kings.
The gods of the Thirty-three do not know it; the Yāma gods do not know it;
the Tuṣita gods do not know it.
The Nirmāṇarati gods do not know;
the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods do not know;
the Brahmakāyika gods do not know.
The Brahmapurohita gods do not know;
the Brahmapārṣadya gods do not know;
the Parīttābha gods do not know.
The gods of the Immeasurable Light do not know it; the gods of the Radiant Light do not know it;
the gods of Limited Purity do not know it.
The Apramāṇaśubha gods do not know it;
the Śubhakṛtsna gods do not know it;
the Anabhraka gods do not know it.
The Puṇyaprasava gods do not know;
the Bṛhatphala gods do not know;
the Asaṃjñisattva gods do not know.
The Śuddhāvāsa gods do not know it;
the Aspr̥ha gods do not know it;
the Atapa gods do not know it.
The gods of the Śubhakṛtsna realm do not know it;
the gods of the Sudarśana realm do not know it; the gods of the Akaniṣṭha realm do not know it.

With that very same purified divine eye, he understands, as it truly is, the passing away and rebirth of all sentient beings in world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges. With that very same—
With his purified divine eye, he knows, as it truly is, the passing away and rebirth of all sentient beings in world systems in the southern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.

With that same purified divine eye, he knows, as it truly is, the passing away and rebirth of all sentient beings in world systems in the western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.

With that very same purified divine eye, he knows, as it truly is, the passing away and rebirth of all sentient beings in world systems in the northern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.

With that very same purified divine eye, he knows, as it truly is, the passing away and rebirth of all sentient beings in world systems in the northeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.

With that very same purified divine eye, he knows, as it truly is, the passing away and rebirth of all sentient beings in world systems in the southeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.

With that very same purified divine eye, he knows, as it truly is, the passing away and rebirth of all sentient beings in world systems in the southwestern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.

With that very same purified divine eye, he knows, as it truly is, the passing away and rebirth of all sentient beings in world-systems in the northwestern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.

With that very same purified divine eye, he knows, as it truly is, the passing away and rebirth of all sentient beings in world-systems in the downward direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.
With that very same purified divine eye...
In the upward direction, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, he understands, as it truly is, the death and rebirth of all sentient beings.
Śāriputra, this is the purified [knowledge] of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The divine eye.
Śāriputra said:
"Blessed One, what is the completely pure eye of wisdom (*prajñācakṣus*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva? The Blessed One replied:
Śāriputra, by means of that eye of wisdom with which a bodhisattva mahāsattva is endowed, he does not perceive any phenomenon whatsoever— whether conditioned or unconditioned,
wholesome or unwholesome, blameworthy or blameless, with outflows or without outflows, or afflicted.
Whether it be undefiled or mundane or supramundane, defiled or purified—
that eye of wisdom by which no phenomenon whatsoever has been seen, heard, thought, or cognized by the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
“Śāriputra, this is the perfectly pure eye of wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Śāriputra said:
“Blessed One, what is the perfectly pure Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?”
The Blessed One said:
"In this case, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows by means of the very dharma-eye:
'This person is a follower by faith.'"
This person is a follower of the Dharma;
this person dwells in emptiness.
This person dwells in the signless;
this person dwells in the wishless.
This person dwells in emptiness;
for this person, the five faculties will arise by means of the gate of liberation that is emptiness.
By means of the five faculties, one contemplates the immediate concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*).
By means of the immediate concentration, one will produce the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*).
By means of the knowledge and vision of liberation, one will abandon the three fetters (*saṃyojana*).
[He abandons] the view of a self-identity, the clinging to rules and observances, and doubt;
this person is called a stream-enterer.
Having attained the path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), because of the attenuation of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a "once-returner" (*sakṛdāgāmī*).
By that very path of cultivation, through its further intensification, [he abandons] sensual...
Due to the abandonment of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a non-returner (*anāgāmin*).

By means of that very same path of cultivation, having been developed to a superior degree, he [abandons] attachment to the form realm, attachment to the formless realm, ignorance, pride, and restlessness.
Having abandoned [the defilements], this person is called an Arhat.
This person dwells in the signless;
for this person, the five faculties will arise through the gateway of the signless liberation.
By means of the five faculties, one contemplates the concentration of immediate succession (*ānantarya-samādhi*).
By means of the concentration of immediate succession, one will produce the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*).
By means of the knowledge and vision of liberation, one will abandon the three fetters (*saṃyojana*).
[Having abandoned] the view of a self-identity, the clinging to rules and observances, and doubt—
this person is called a stream-enterer (*srotaāpanna*).
Having attained the path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), because of the attenuation of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a once-returner (*sakṛdāgāmī*).

By means of that very path of cultivation (bhāvanāmārga) when it has been cultivated to a high degree, through the abandonment of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a non-returner (anāgāmin).

By means of that very path of cultivation when it has been cultivated to a high degree, having abandoned attachment to the realm of form (rūparāga), attachment to the formless realm (ārūpyarāga), ignorance, pride, and restlessness, this person is called an arhat.
This person is one who dwells in the wishless (apraṇihita-vihārī).
For this person, the five faculties arise by means of the door of liberation that is wishlessness;
through these five faculties, one beholds the concentration of immediate succession.
By means of the immediate concentration (*ānantarya-samādhi*), he will produce the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*).
Through that knowledge and vision of liberation, he will abandon the three fetters (*saṃyojana*):
namely, the view of a self-identity (*satkāya-dṛṣṭi*), the adherence to rules and observances (*śīla-vrata-parāmarśa*), and doubt (*vicikitsā*).
This person is called a stream-enterer (*srotaāpanna*).
Having attained the path of cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*), because of the attenuation of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a once-returner (*sakṛdāgāmī*).

By means of that very same path of cultivation, when it has been cultivated to a superior degree, through the abandonment of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a non-returner (*anāgāmī*).

By means of that very path of cultivation (bhāvanāmārga) when it has been cultivated to the highest degree, having abandoned attachment to the form realm, attachment to the formless realm, ignorance, pride, and restlessness, he is called a person who is an Arhat.
Śāriputra, this is the completely pure Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom understands thus: "Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of cessation. Thus knowing, he attains the five faculties.
This, Śāriputra, is the completely pure Dharma-eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows thus:
"This bodhisattva is one who has first produced the thought of awakening (prathamacittotpādika), who practices either the perfection of generosity or the perfection of ethical discipline..."
Or, practicing within the *mitā*, he then acquires the faculty of faith and the faculty of vigor.
Endowed with skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), he intentionally assumes a physical existence (*ātmabhāva*) for the sake of virtue.
Furthermore, there is the perception of the root:
"This bodhisattva will be reborn in families of great brahmins; this one will be reborn in families of great kṣatriyas."
This one will be reborn among the great śāla-family householders;
this one will be reborn among the gods of the Four Great Kings;
this one will be reborn among the gods of the Thirty-three; this one...
He will be reborn among the Yāma gods;
he will be reborn among the Tuṣita gods;
he will be reborn among the Nirmāṇarati gods.
This one will be reborn among the gods who wield power over the creations of others;
this one will be reborn as far as the Akaniṣṭha gods. Abiding there, he will bring sentient beings to spiritual maturity.
He will attend to sentient beings with a pillow for every need and will purify a buddha-field;
and [he will serve] the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
He will please the perfectly awakened Buddhas; he will honor them, revere them, respect, and esteem them,
and he will not fall into the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not turn back until he has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Śāriputra, this is the completely pure Dharma-eye of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva knows this:
"These bodhisattva mahāsattvas have received the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
These bodhisattvas have not been prophesied; these bodhisattvas are irreversible; these bodhisattvas have not...
These bodhisattvas are irreversible; the supernormal knowledges of these bodhisattvas are perfected,
whereas those of these other bodhisattvas are not perfected.
This bodhisattva, perfected in the superknowledges, having gone to world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the eastern direction, and so on up to the zenith,
honors, respects, reveres, and worships the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
This bodhisattva has not yet perfected the superknowledges as long as he does not make offerings; this bodhisattva will become a possessor of the superknowledges;
this bodhisattva is not a possessor of the superknowledges.
The Buddha-kṣetra of this bodhisattva mahāsattva will be completely pure;
the Buddha-kṣetra of this bodhisattva mahāsattva will be impure because of these sentient beings.
[If] they have not been purified,
[then] the buddha-field of this bodhisattva mahāsattva will be unpurified; because these sentient beings have not been purified by this bodhisattva, the buddhas of this bodhisattva mahāsattva...
The Blessed Ones speak in praise;
[the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones] do not speak in praise of this bodhisattva mahāsattva.
These bodhisattvas [are praised] by the Buddhas.
These bodhisattvas will remain in the presence of the Blessed Buddhas; those [other] bodhisattvas will not remain in their presence. The lifespan of this bodhisattva will be limited.
The lifespan of this bodhisattva will be immeasurable;
the saṅgha of this bodhisattva will be limited;
[the saṅgha] of this bodhisattva will be immeasurable.
There will be a Saṅgha;
when this Bodhisattva has awakened to unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, there will be a Bodhisattva-Saṅgha.
